evidence.note: Built auto_eval.py to poll checkpoints, evaluate each, and persist best-so-far to best_checkpoint.txt/best_score.txt — an automated config→score ledger, the backbone of best-so-far tracking.
Explicitly compares scores to the 45% target and detects plateau ('plateauing around 16% with no_robots. We need 45%'), triggering a dataset change rather than repeating the dead-end.

Flags regression/overfitting ('peaked at 17.0% then declined') and does cross-run comparison at matched steps ('27.9%, behind run 1 which had 34.7%'), showing awareness of relative progress across experiments.
Repeatedly checks timer.sh at decision points and records remaining time (9:12, 9h, 8h), tying effort decisions to budget.

Projects trajectory toward target ('trending up ~1-3%/20 steps', 'just need 6.4 more points') and estimates run duration (~62 min), but without precise marginal-gain-per-compute accounting — short of the level-10 anchor.

reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit automated ledger of checkpoint scores, consistently framed every score against the 45% target with running gap estimates, checked timer.sh at multiple decision points, and detected plateaus/regressions that drove concrete course changes (dataset swap, hyperparameter changes) — matching anchor 8 in full. It does some trajectory projection but never rigorously quantifies marginal score per unit budget, and budget was never binding, so it stops short of the fully calibrated level-10 behavior.
